abstract: The author outlines the special features of Manchester's Metrolink which have influenced the associated electrical and mechanical works. The author then describes the light rail vehicles, the signalling, power supply and overhead line equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Telecommunications systems on the Manchester Metrolink
abstract: The Manchester Metrolink Light Rail System requires good telecommunication systems to ensure the safe and efficient running of the railway. The focal point for communications is at the Queens Road control centre which lies geographically towards the centre of the present railway network. An optical fibre transmission system and trunked radio system enable communications to be extended from the control centre to stations and light rail vehicles respectively. On-board communications between drivers and passengers are also provided. The author describes each of these systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Metrolink: the long road from paper studies to tender evaluation
abstract: The author briefly discusses the problems of public transport in Manchester which led to the idea of Metrolink. The basic requirements of the Metrolink are listed. The author discusses the Parliamentary Bills and application for grant-aid relating to the Metrolink. The author then discusses the tendering process for the main contract.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Manchester Metrolink-vehicle propulsion and auxiliary system
abstract: The two car articulated Metrolink vehicles are powered by four separately excited DC traction motors. The motors are arranged in a two series two parallel configuration, each series armature string being controlled by an independent chopper. The vehicle HV auxiliary loads-the heating and compressor circuits are fed directly from the line at 750 V. The LV auxiliary loads-the vehicle control circuit, lighting circuits and track brake magnets are supplied from a static auxiliary converter. The auxiliary converter also supplies the motor field circuits. The propulsion and auxiliary systems use the latest control technologies applied to a proven power system. The propulsion and auxiliary converters are microprocessor controlled and use gate turn off thyristors (GTOs) in the power circuit. The auxiliary converter also uses insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) in its outputs which offer advantages for lower power switching applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The civil engineering aspects of Metrolink
abstract: During late 1989 the GMA group won the contract to design, build, operate and maintain the Manchester Metrolink. The GMA group is a nonintegrated joint venture partnership consisting of; GEC-Alsthom, Mowlem Civil Engineering, AMEC, and GM Buses. The author briefly discusses the civil engineering work carried out for the five sections of Metrolink. These sections are: the city centre, viaducts, British Rail lines, Piccadilly Undercroft, and Victoria station. The work included track laying, overhead line installation and structural repairs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

The author describes the three components of the signalling system: vital signalling, vehicle recognition system, and centralised control and supervision system. The vital signalling covers the segregated sections and uses a solid state interlocking system. The vehicle recognition system is used to control the street running section and uses both trainborne and trackside equipment to control special traffic lights. The centralised control and supervision system uses the SIGNET system, developed by GEC ALSTHOM, to control the signalling system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
